meta.cover: Covers every section in force, chapter by chapter, including Chapter XVII on cheque bounce (S.138–148).

items.head: Short title, local extent; saving of usages relating to hundis
items.group: Chapter I — Preliminary
items.gist: The Act may be called the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881 and extends to the whole of India. Nothing in it affects the Indian Paper Currency Act or any local usage relating to instruments in an oriental language (hundis), unless the instrument shows the parties intended the Act to govern it.

items.head: Interpretation — 'banker'
items.group: Chapter I — Preliminary
items.gist: 'Banker' includes any person acting as a banker and any post office savings bank.

items.head: Promissory note
items.group: Chapter II — Of notes, bills and cheques
items.gist: An instrument in writing (not a bank-note or currency-note) containing an unconditional undertaking, signed by the maker, to pay a certain sum of money only to, or to the order of, a certain person, or to the bearer. A mere acknowledgment of debt (IOU), a conditional promise or an uncertain sum is not a promissory note.

items.head: Bill of exchange
items.group: Chapter II — Of notes, bills and cheques
items.gist: An instrument in writing containing an unconditional order, signed by the maker, directing a certain person to pay a certain sum of money only to, or to the order of, a certain person or to the bearer.

items.head: Cheque
items.group: Chapter II — Of notes, bills and cheques
items.gist: A bill of exchange drawn on a specified banker and not expressed to be payable otherwise than on demand; includes the electronic image of a truncated cheque and a cheque in electronic form.

items.head: Drawer, drawee, acceptor, payee
items.group: Chapter II — Of notes, bills and cheques
items.gist: The maker of a bill or cheque is the drawer; the person directed to pay is the drawee; a drawee who accepts is the acceptor; the person to whom (or to whose order) the money is payable is the payee. A 'drawee in case of need' may be named in the bill or an endorsement.

items.head: Holder
items.group: Chapter II — Of notes, bills and cheques
items.gist: The person entitled in his own name to possession of the instrument and to receive or recover the amount due on it from the parties.

items.head: Holder in due course
items.group: Chapter II — Of notes, bills and cheques
items.gist: A person who, for consideration, became the possessor (bearer instrument) or payee or endorsee (order instrument) before the amount became payable, without sufficient cause to believe there was any defect in the title of the person from whom he derived his title.

items.head: Payment in due course
items.group: Chapter II — Of notes, bills and cheques
items.gist: Payment in accordance with the apparent tenor of the instrument, in good faith and without negligence, to any person in possession of it, in circumstances which do not give reasonable ground to believe he is not entitled to receive payment.

items.head: Inland instrument
items.group: Chapter II — Of notes, bills and cheques
items.gist: A note, bill or cheque drawn or made in India and made payable in, or drawn upon any person resident in, India.

items.head: Foreign instrument
items.group: Chapter II — Of notes, bills and cheques
items.gist: Any instrument which is not an inland instrument.

items.head: Negotiable instrument
items.group: Chapter II — Of notes, bills and cheques
items.gist: A promissory note, bill of exchange or cheque payable either to order or to bearer. An instrument payable to a named person without words prohibiting transfer is payable to order. It may be made payable to two or more payees jointly or in the alternative.

items.head: Negotiation
items.group: Chapter II — Of notes, bills and cheques
items.gist: When an instrument is transferred to any person so as to make that person its holder, it is said to be negotiated.

items.head: Indorsement
items.group: Chapter II — Of notes, bills and cheques
items.gist: When the maker or holder signs on the instrument (or on a slip attached — an allonge) for the purpose of negotiation, he is said to indorse it; he is the indorser.

items.head: Indorsement in blank and in full
items.group: Chapter II — Of notes, bills and cheques
items.gist: Signature alone is an indorsement in blank (instrument becomes payable to bearer); if it names the person to whom or to whose order it is to be paid, it is an indorsement in full.

items.head: Ambiguous instruments
items.group: Chapter II — Of notes, bills and cheques
items.gist: Where an instrument may be construed either as a promissory note or a bill of exchange, the holder may at his election treat it as either, and it is thereafter treated accordingly.

items.head: Where amount is stated differently in figures and words
items.group: Chapter II — Of notes, bills and cheques
items.gist: If the amount in words and in figures differ, the amount stated in words is the amount undertaken or ordered to be paid.

items.head: Instruments payable on demand
items.group: Chapter II — Of notes, bills and cheques
items.gist: A note or bill in which no time for payment is specified, and a cheque, are payable on demand.

items.head: Inchoate stamped instruments
items.group: Chapter II — Of notes, bills and cheques
items.gist: A person who signs and delivers a blank or incomplete stamped paper gives the holder prima facie authority to complete it for any amount not exceeding that covered by the stamp; he is liable to a holder in due course for that amount, but others can recover only the amount intended.

items.head: 'At sight', 'on presentment', 'after sight'
items.group: Chapter II — Of notes, bills and cheques
items.gist: 'At sight' and 'on presentment' mean on demand; 'after sight' means, in a note, after presentment for sight, and in a bill, after acceptance (or noting/protest for non-acceptance).

items.head: Maturity; days of grace
items.group: Chapter II — Of notes, bills and cheques
items.gist: Maturity is the date on which the instrument falls due. Every instrument payable otherwise than on demand is due on the third day after the day it is expressed to be payable — three days of grace.

items.head: Calculating maturity — months
items.group: Chapter II — Of notes, bills and cheques
items.gist: For instruments payable so many months after date or sight, the period ends on the corresponding day of the month; if there is none, on the last day of that month.

items.head: Calculating maturity — days
items.group: Chapter II — Of notes, bills and cheques
items.gist: For instruments payable so many days after date or sight or after an event, the day of the date, presentment, protest or event is excluded.

items.head: When day of maturity is a holiday
items.group: Chapter II — Of notes, bills and cheques
items.gist: If the day of maturity is a public holiday, the instrument is deemed due on the next preceding business day.

items.head: Capacity to make, etc.
items.group: Chapter III — Parties to notes, bills and cheques
items.gist: Every person capable of contracting may bind himself by making, drawing, accepting, indorsing, delivering and negotiating an instrument. A minor may draw, indorse, deliver and negotiate so as to bind all parties except himself.

items.head: Agency
items.group: Chapter III — Parties to notes, bills and cheques
items.gist: A person may bind himself through a duly authorised agent; general authority to transact business and receive debts does not by itself authorise accepting or indorsing bills.

items.head: Liability of agent signing
items.group: Chapter III — Parties to notes, bills and cheques
items.gist: An agent who signs without indicating that he signs as agent, or that he does not intend to incur personal responsibility, is personally liable — except to those who induced him to sign believing only the principal would be liable.

items.head: Liability of legal representative signing
items.group: Chapter III — Parties to notes, bills and cheques
items.gist: A legal representative of a deceased person who signs an instrument in his own name is personally liable unless he expressly limits his liability to the assets received.

items.head: Liability of drawer
items.group: Chapter III — Parties to notes, bills and cheques
items.gist: The drawer of a bill or cheque must compensate the holder if it is dishonoured, provided due notice of dishonour has been given or received.

items.head: Liability of drawee of cheque
items.group: Chapter III — Parties to notes, bills and cheques
items.gist: A drawee banker having sufficient funds of the drawer properly applicable must pay the cheque when duly required, and must compensate the drawer for loss caused by default.

items.head: Liability of maker of note and acceptor of bill
items.group: Chapter III — Parties to notes, bills and cheques
items.gist: The maker of a note and the acceptor of a bill are bound to pay the amount at maturity according to the apparent tenor (or of the acceptance), and to compensate for default.

items.head: Only drawee can be acceptor
items.group: Chapter III — Parties to notes, bills and cheques
items.gist: No person except the drawee (or all or some of several drawees, a drawee in case of need, or an acceptor for honour) can bind himself by accepting.

items.head: Acceptance by several drawees not partners
items.group: Chapter III — Parties to notes, bills and cheques
items.gist: Where there are several drawees who are not partners, each may accept for himself, but none can accept for another without authority.

items.head: Liability of indorser
items.group: Chapter III — Parties to notes, bills and cheques
items.gist: An indorser, in the absence of a contract to the contrary, is bound to compensate every subsequent holder on dishonour, provided due notice of dishonour is given.

items.head: Liability of prior parties to holder in due course
items.group: Chapter III — Parties to notes, bills and cheques
items.gist: Every prior party is liable to a holder in due course until the instrument is duly satisfied.

items.head: Maker, drawer and acceptor principals
items.group: Chapter III — Parties to notes, bills and cheques
items.gist: The maker of a note or cheque, the drawer of a bill until acceptance, and the acceptor are, in the absence of a contrary contract, liable as principal debtors; other parties are liable as sureties.

items.head: Prior party a principal in respect of each subsequent party
items.group: Chapter III — Parties to notes, bills and cheques
items.gist: As between the parties liable as sureties, each prior party is liable as principal debtor in respect of each subsequent party.

items.head: Suretyship
items.group: Chapter III — Parties to notes, bills and cheques
items.gist: Where the holder of an accepted bill makes a contract with the acceptor that would discharge the other parties, he may expressly reserve his right to charge them, and then they are not discharged.

items.head: Discharge of indorser's liability
items.group: Chapter III — Parties to notes, bills and cheques
items.gist: If the holder, without the indorser's consent, destroys or impairs the indorser's remedy against a prior party, the indorser is discharged to the same extent as a surety.

items.head: Acceptor bound although indorsement forged
items.group: Chapter III — Parties to notes, bills and cheques
items.gist: An acceptor of a bill already indorsed is not relieved from liability because an indorsement is forged, if he knew or had reason to believe it was forged when he accepted.

items.head: Acceptance of bill drawn in fictitious name
items.group: Chapter III — Parties to notes, bills and cheques
items.gist: An acceptor of a bill drawn in a fictitious name and payable to the drawer's order is not relieved from liability to a holder in due course who claims under an indorsement in the same handwriting as the drawer's signature.

items.head: Instrument made without consideration
items.group: Chapter III — Parties to notes, bills and cheques
items.gist: An instrument made, drawn, accepted, indorsed or transferred without consideration, or for a consideration that fails, creates no obligation between the parties to that transaction; but if a party transfers it for consideration, the transferee and later holders may recover from any prior party.

items.head: Partial absence or failure of money consideration
items.group: Chapter III — Parties to notes, bills and cheques
items.gist: Where the consideration consists of money and is partly absent or fails, the sum recoverable between the immediate parties is reduced proportionately.

items.head: Partial failure of consideration not consisting of money
items.group: Chapter III — Parties to notes, bills and cheques
items.gist: Where the consideration is not money and fails partly but can be ascertained, the sum recoverable is reduced proportionately.

items.head: Holder's right to duplicate of lost bill
items.group: Chapter III — Parties to notes, bills and cheques
items.gist: Where a bill is lost before it is overdue, the holder may require the drawer to give another bill of the same tenor, on giving security against loss if the lost bill is found.

items.head: Delivery
items.group: Chapter IV — Of negotiation
items.gist: Making, acceptance or indorsement is completed by delivery, actual or constructive. Delivery may be conditional or for a special purpose only, and the property in the instrument does not then pass.

items.head: Negotiation by delivery
items.group: Chapter IV — Of negotiation
items.gist: An instrument payable to bearer is negotiable by delivery.

items.head: Negotiation by indorsement
items.group: Chapter IV — Of negotiation
items.gist: An instrument payable to order is negotiable by the holder by indorsement and delivery.

items.head: Conversion of indorsement in blank into indorsement in full
items.group: Chapter IV — Of negotiation
items.gist: The holder of an instrument indorsed in blank may, without signing, convert it into an indorsement in full by writing a direction to pay to himself or another person.

items.head: Effect of indorsement
items.group: Chapter IV — Of negotiation
items.gist: An indorsement followed by delivery transfers the property in the instrument with the right of further negotiation — but the indorsement may restrict or exclude further negotiation, or constitute the indorsee an agent (e.g. 'for collection').

items.head: Who may negotiate
items.group: Chapter IV — Of negotiation
items.gist: Every sole maker, drawer, payee or indorsee, or all of several joint ones, may negotiate, provided the instrument is negotiable.

items.head: Indorser who excludes his liability or makes it conditional
items.group: Chapter IV — Of negotiation
items.gist: An indorser may by express words exclude his own liability (sans recours) or make his liability, or the indorsee's right to receive, depend on a specified event, although the event may never happen.

items.head: Holder deriving title from holder in due course
items.group: Chapter IV — Of negotiation
items.gist: A holder who derives title from a holder in due course has the rights of that holder in due course.

items.head: Instrument indorsed in blank
items.group: Chapter IV — Of negotiation
items.gist: An instrument indorsed in blank is payable to bearer and may be negotiated by delivery, unless converted into an indorsement in full.

items.head: Conversion of indorsement in blank into indorsement in full
items.group: Chapter IV — Of negotiation
items.gist: If an instrument indorsed in blank is later indorsed in full, the amount cannot be claimed from the indorser in full except by the person to whom it was indorsed in full or one who derives title through him.

items.head: Indorsement for part of sum due
items.group: Chapter IV — Of negotiation
items.gist: An indorsement transferring only part of the amount is not valid for negotiation; but where part has been paid, that may be noted and the instrument negotiated for the balance.

items.head: Legal representative cannot negotiate by delivery only
items.group: Chapter IV — Of negotiation
items.gist: The legal representative of a deceased holder of an order instrument which the deceased had delivered without indorsing cannot negotiate it by delivery alone.

items.head: Instrument obtained by unlawful means or for unlawful consideration
items.group: Chapter IV — Of negotiation
items.gist: If an instrument is lost or obtained by an offence or fraud or for unlawful consideration, no possessor or indorsee claiming through the wrongdoer can recover on it — unless he (or a person through whom he claims) is a holder in due course.

items.head: Instrument acquired after dishonour or when overdue
items.group: Chapter IV — Of negotiation
items.gist: A person who takes an instrument after dishonour or when overdue, with notice, gets only the title of his transferor (subject to equities); an accommodation instrument may be enforced by a person who took it for consideration after maturity against the accommodating party.

items.head: Instrument negotiable till payment or satisfaction
items.group: Chapter IV — Of negotiation
items.gist: An instrument may be negotiated until it has been paid or satisfied by the maker, drawee or acceptor at or after maturity, but not after such payment or satisfaction.

items.head: Presentment for acceptance
items.group: Chapter V — Of presentment
items.gist: A bill payable after sight must, if no time or place is specified, be presented to the drawee for acceptance within a reasonable time after it is drawn; if not, no party is liable to the person making the default.

items.head: Presentment of promissory note for sight
items.group: Chapter V — Of presentment
items.gist: A note payable at a certain period after sight must be presented to the maker for sight (if he can be found) within a reasonable time.

items.head: Drawee's time for deliberation
items.group: Chapter V — Of presentment
items.gist: The holder must allow the drawee 48 hours (exclusive of public holidays) to consider whether he will accept.

items.head: Presentment for payment
items.group: Chapter V — Of presentment
items.gist: Instruments must be presented for payment to the maker, acceptor or drawee by or on behalf of the holder; in default, the other parties are not liable to the holder. A truncated cheque may be presented as its electronic image.

items.head: Hours for presentment
items.group: Chapter V — Of presentment
items.gist: Presentment for payment must be made during the usual hours of business, and at banking places within banking hours.

items.head: Presentment for payment of instrument payable after date or sight
items.group: Chapter V — Of presentment
items.gist: Such instruments must be presented for payment at maturity.

items.head: Presentment for payment of promissory note payable by instalments
items.group: Chapter V — Of presentment
items.gist: A note payable by instalments must be presented for payment on the third day after the date fixed for payment of each instalment; non-payment on such presentment has the same effect as non-payment at maturity.

items.head: Presentment at specified place
items.group: Chapter V — Of presentment
items.gist: An instrument made payable at a specified place, and not elsewhere, must be presented there to charge any party.

items.head: Instrument payable at specified place
items.group: Chapter V — Of presentment
items.gist: An instrument made payable at a specified place must be presented there to charge the maker or drawer.

items.head: Presentment where no exclusive place specified
items.group: Chapter V — Of presentment
items.gist: Where no place of payment is specified, presentment is made at the place of business or usual residence of the maker, drawee or acceptor.

items.head: Presentment when maker has no known place of business or residence
items.group: Chapter V — Of presentment
items.gist: Then presentment may be made to him in person wherever he can be found.

items.head: Presentment of cheque to charge drawer
items.group: Chapter V — Of presentment
items.gist: A cheque must be presented at the bank on which it is drawn before the relation between the drawer and his banker has been altered to the prejudice of the drawer.

items.head: Presentment of cheque to charge any other person
items.group: Chapter V — Of presentment
items.gist: To charge any person other than the drawer, a cheque must be presented within a reasonable time after delivery by that person.

items.head: Presentment of instrument payable on demand
items.group: Chapter V — Of presentment
items.gist: A note payable on demand must be presented within a reasonable time after it is received by the holder.

items.head: Presentment by or to agent, representative of deceased, or assignee of insolvent
items.group: Chapter V — Of presentment
items.gist: Presentment may be made to the duly authorised agent of the maker, drawee or acceptor, or, if he is dead, to his legal representative, or, if insolvent, to his assignee.

items.head: Excuse for delay in presentment for acceptance or payment
items.group: Chapter V — Of presentment
items.gist: Delay is excused if caused by circumstances beyond the holder's control and not due to his default, misconduct or negligence; presentment must be made with reasonable diligence once the cause ceases.

items.head: When presentment unnecessary
items.group: Chapter V — Of presentment
items.gist: Presentment is unnecessary if the maker, drawee or acceptor intentionally prevents it; if his business place is closed or no one is there to pay; if he cannot be found after due search; if he has promised to pay notwithstanding non-presentment; if payment would be refused anyway; or as against a party who could not suffer damage.

items.head: Liability of banker for negligently dealing with bill presented for payment
items.group: Chapter V — Of presentment
items.gist: A banker who negligently loses or damages a bill delivered to him for presentment for payment is liable to compensate the holder.

items.head: To whom payment should be made
items.group: Chapter VI — Of payment and interest
items.gist: Payment must be made to the holder of the instrument to discharge the maker or acceptor.

items.head: Interest when rate specified
items.group: Chapter VI — Of payment and interest
items.gist: Where interest at a specified rate is expressly made payable, it is calculated at that rate from the date of the instrument until tender or realisation; after a suit, at such rate as the court directs.

items.head: Interest when no rate specified
items.group: Chapter VI — Of payment and interest
items.gist: When no rate is specified, interest on the amount due is calculated at 18 per cent per annum from the date it ought to have been paid.

items.head: Delivery of instrument on payment, or indemnity in case of loss
items.group: Chapter VI — Of payment and interest
items.gist: The person paying is entitled to have the instrument delivered up to him; if it is lost, to be indemnified against further claims.

items.head: Discharge from liability
items.group: Chapter VII — Of discharge from liability on notes, bills and cheques
items.gist: A party is discharged (a) by cancellation of his name by the holder with intent to discharge him; (b) by release; (c) by payment of the amount due by the maker, drawee or acceptor at or after maturity, or by the drawee of a cheque in due course.

items.head: Discharge by allowing drawee more than 48 hours to accept
items.group: Chapter VII — Of discharge from liability on notes, bills and cheques
items.gist: If the holder allows the drawee more than 48 hours to consider acceptance, all previous parties not consenting are discharged from liability to him.

items.head: When cheque not duly presented and drawer damaged thereby
items.group: Chapter VII — Of discharge from liability on notes, bills and cheques
items.gist: If a cheque is not presented within a reasonable time and the drawer suffers actual damage through the delay (e.g. the bank fails), he is discharged to the extent of that damage; the holder becomes a creditor of the bank in place of the drawer.

items.head: Cheque payable to order / to bearer
items.group: Chapter VII — Of discharge from liability on notes, bills and cheques
items.gist: (1) A drawee who pays an order cheque purporting to be indorsed by the payee in due course is discharged. (2) A cheque originally expressed payable to bearer is discharged by payment in due course to the bearer, notwithstanding any indorsement on it.

items.head: Drafts drawn by one branch of a bank on another payable to order
items.group: Chapter VII — Of discharge from liability on notes, bills and cheques
items.gist: A bank paying in due course a draft drawn by one of its offices on another, payable to order and purporting to be indorsed by the payee, is discharged.

items.head: Parties not consenting discharged by qualified or limited acceptance
items.group: Chapter VII — Of discharge from liability on notes, bills and cheques
items.gist: If the holder takes a qualified acceptance (conditional, for part of the sum, at a different place — 'only and not elsewhere' — or time), prior parties who do not consent are discharged.

items.head: Effect of material alteration
items.group: Chapter VII — Of discharge from liability on notes, bills and cheques
items.gist: A material alteration renders the instrument void as against any party who did not consent to it, unless made to carry out the common intention of the original parties; an alteration by an indorsee discharges his indorser.

items.head: Acceptor or indorser bound notwithstanding previous alteration
items.group: Chapter VII — Of discharge from liability on notes, bills and cheques
items.gist: An acceptor or indorser is bound by his acceptance or indorsement notwithstanding any previous alteration of the instrument.

items.head: Payment of instrument on which alteration is not apparent
items.group: Chapter VII — Of discharge from liability on notes, bills and cheques
items.gist: Where an instrument has been materially altered but does not appear to be altered, payment in due course according to its apparent tenor discharges the payer; a banker paying such a cheque may debit the customer.

items.head: Extinguishment of rights of action on bill in acceptor's hands
items.group: Chapter VII — Of discharge from liability on notes, bills and cheques
items.gist: If a negotiated bill is held by the acceptor in his own right at or after maturity, all rights of action on it are extinguished.

items.head: Dishonour by non-acceptance
items.group: Chapter VIII — Of notice of dishonour
items.gist: A bill is dishonoured by non-acceptance when the drawee makes default in accepting after due presentment, or gives a qualified acceptance, or where presentment is excused and the bill is not accepted.

items.head: Dishonour by non-payment
items.group: Chapter VIII — Of notice of dishonour
items.gist: An instrument is dishonoured by non-payment when the maker, acceptor or drawee makes default in payment upon being duly required to pay.

items.head: By and to whom notice should be given
items.group: Chapter VIII — Of notice of dishonour
items.gist: The holder (or a party liable) must give notice of dishonour to all other parties whom he seeks to make liable; it is not necessary to give it to the maker of a note or acceptor of a bill or drawee of a cheque.

items.head: Mode in which notice may be given
items.group: Chapter VIII — Of notice of dishonour
items.gist: Notice may be oral or written, by post or otherwise; it must inform the party of the dishonour; it must be given within a reasonable time at the party's place of business or residence.

items.head: Party receiving must transmit notice of dishonour
items.group: Chapter VIII — Of notice of dishonour
items.gist: A party receiving notice must, to render prior parties liable to him, give notice to them within a reasonable time.

items.head: Agent for presentment
items.group: Chapter VIII — Of notice of dishonour
items.gist: An agent who presented the instrument may give notice to his principal, who may then give notice to prior parties.

items.head: When party to whom notice given is dead
items.group: Chapter VIII — Of notice of dishonour
items.gist: Notice given to a party after his death in ignorance of it is sufficient.

items.head: When notice of dishonour is unnecessary
items.group: Chapter VIII — Of notice of dishonour
items.gist: Notice is unnecessary when dispensed with by the party; to charge the drawer when he has countermanded payment; when the party could not suffer damage; when the party cannot be found after due search; when the omission is caused by unavoidable circumstances; when the acceptor is also the drawer; for a promissory note which is not negotiable; or when the party, knowing the facts, promises unconditionally to pay.

items.head: Noting
items.group: Chapter IX — Of noting and protest
items.gist: When an instrument is dishonoured, the holder may cause it to be noted by a notary public on the instrument (or a paper attached) — recording the fact of dishonour, the date, the reason and the notary's charges — within a reasonable time.

items.head: Protest
items.group: Chapter IX — Of noting and protest
items.gist: The holder may have a notary certify the dishonour; this certificate is a protest. Protest for better security may be made when the acceptor becomes insolvent or suspends payment before maturity.

items.head: Contents of protest
items.group: Chapter IX — Of noting and protest
items.gist: A protest contains the instrument or a copy, the names of parties, the fact and reasons of dishonour, the place and time, and the notary's signature.

items.head: Notice of protest
items.group: Chapter IX — Of noting and protest
items.gist: When a protest is required by law, notice of the protest must be given in the same manner as notice of dishonour.

items.head: Protest for non-payment after dishonour by non-acceptance
items.group: Chapter IX — Of noting and protest
items.gist: All bills dishonoured by non-acceptance may be protested for non-payment as well.

items.head: Protest of foreign bills
items.group: Chapter IX — Of noting and protest
items.gist: Foreign bills must be protested for dishonour when such protest is required by the law of the place where they are drawn.

items.head: When noting equivalent to protest
items.group: Chapter IX — Of noting and protest
items.gist: If a bill or note is noted within the required time, the protest may be completed later, dated as of the date of noting.

items.head: Reasonable time
items.group: Chapter X — Of reasonable time
items.gist: In determining reasonable time for presentment, notice of dishonour or noting, regard is had to the nature of the instrument and the usual course of dealing; public holidays are excluded.

items.head: Reasonable time of giving notice of dishonour
items.group: Chapter X — Of reasonable time
items.gist: If the holder and the party to be notified carry on business or live in different places, notice is in reasonable time if sent by the next post; if in the same place, if it reaches him before the close of business the next day.

items.head: Reasonable time for transmitting notice
items.group: Chapter X — Of reasonable time
items.gist: A party receiving notice must transmit it within the same reasonable time.

items.head: Acceptance for honour
items.group: Chapter XI — Acceptance and payment for honour; reference in case of need
items.gist: When a bill has been noted or protested for non-acceptance or better security, any person not already liable may, with the holder's consent, accept it for the honour of any party.

items.head: How acceptance for honour must be made
items.group: Chapter XI — Acceptance and payment for honour; reference in case of need
items.gist: By writing on the bill words indicating acceptance for honour, signed by the acceptor.

items.head: Acceptance not specifying for whose honour
items.group: Chapter XI — Acceptance and payment for honour; reference in case of need
items.gist: It is deemed made for the honour of the drawer.

items.head: Liability of acceptor for honour
items.group: Chapter XI — Acceptance and payment for honour; reference in case of need
items.gist: He is liable to all parties subsequent to the party for whose honour he accepted.

items.head: When acceptor for honour may be charged
items.group: Chapter XI — Acceptance and payment for honour; reference in case of need
items.gist: Only if the bill has been duly presented for payment to the drawee at maturity and protested for non-payment, and notice given to him.

items.head: Payment for honour
items.group: Chapter XI — Acceptance and payment for honour; reference in case of need
items.gist: When a bill has been protested for non-payment, any person may pay it for the honour of any party liable.

items.head: Right of payer for honour
items.group: Chapter XI — Acceptance and payment for honour; reference in case of need
items.gist: He acquires the holder's rights against the party for whose honour he paid and all prior parties.

items.head: Drawee in case of need
items.group: Chapter XI — Acceptance and payment for honour; reference in case of need
items.gist: Where a drawee in case of need is named, the bill is not dishonoured until it has been dishonoured by him.

items.head: Acceptance and payment without protest
items.group: Chapter XI — Acceptance and payment for honour; reference in case of need
items.gist: A drawee in case of need may accept and pay without protest.

items.head: Rules as to compensation
items.group: Chapter XII — Of compensation
items.gist: On dishonour the holder is entitled to the amount due with expenses of presenting, noting and protesting; re-exchange rules apply where parties are in different places; an indorser who pays may recover the amount paid with interest at 18 per cent from the date of payment, and expenses.

items.head: Presumptions as to negotiable instruments
items.group: Chapter XIII — Special rules of evidence
items.gist: Until the contrary is proved it is presumed: (a) consideration; (b) date; (c) acceptance within reasonable time and before maturity; (d) transfer before maturity; (e) indorsements in the order they appear; (f) a lost instrument was duly stamped; (g) the holder is a holder in due course — but if the instrument was obtained by offence, fraud or unlawful consideration, the burden of proving holder-in-due-course status is on the holder.

items.head: Presumption on proof of protest
items.group: Chapter XIII — Special rules of evidence
items.gist: In a suit on a dishonoured instrument, on proof of protest the court presumes the fact of dishonour unless disproved.

items.head: Estoppel against denying original validity
items.group: Chapter XIII — Special rules of evidence
items.gist: No maker, drawer, or acceptor for honour can, in a suit by a holder in due course, deny the validity of the instrument as originally made or drawn.

items.head: Estoppel against denying capacity of payee to indorse
items.group: Chapter XIII — Special rules of evidence
items.gist: No maker of a note or acceptor of a bill payable to order can, in a suit by a holder in due course, deny the payee's capacity at the date of the instrument to indorse it.

items.head: Estoppel against denying signature or capacity of prior party
items.group: Chapter XIII — Special rules of evidence
items.gist: No indorser can, in a suit by a subsequent holder, deny the signature or capacity of any prior party.

items.head: Cheque crossed generally
items.group: Chapter XIV — Of crossed cheques
items.gist: Two transverse parallel lines across the face, with or without 'and company' (or an abbreviation) and with or without 'not negotiable'.

items.head: Cheque crossed specially
items.group: Chapter XIV — Of crossed cheques
items.gist: The name of a banker added across the face, with or without 'not negotiable'.

items.head: Crossing after issue
items.group: Chapter XIV — Of crossed cheques
items.gist: The holder may cross an uncrossed cheque generally or specially, convert a general crossing into special, and add 'not negotiable'; a banker to whom it is crossed specially may cross it again to another banker as his agent for collection; a collecting banker may cross an uncrossed or generally crossed cheque to himself.

items.head: Payment of cheque crossed generally / specially
items.group: Chapter XIV — Of crossed cheques
items.gist: A generally crossed cheque is paid only to a banker; a specially crossed cheque only to the banker named or his agent for collection.

items.head: Payment of cheque crossed specially more than once
items.group: Chapter XIV — Of crossed cheques
items.gist: If crossed specially to more than one banker (except to an agent for collection), the drawee shall refuse payment.

items.head: Payment in due course of crossed cheque
items.group: Chapter XIV — Of crossed cheques
items.gist: A banker paying a crossed cheque in good faith and without negligence according to the crossing — and the drawer, if the cheque reached the payee — are in the same position as if the true owner had been paid.

items.head: Payment of crossed cheque out of due course
items.group: Chapter XIV — Of crossed cheques
items.gist: A banker who pays a crossed cheque otherwise than in accordance with the crossing is liable to the true owner for any resulting loss.

items.head: Cheque bearing 'not negotiable'
items.group: Chapter XIV — Of crossed cheques
items.gist: A person taking a cheque crossed generally or specially and bearing 'not negotiable' does not get, and cannot give, a better title than that of the person from whom he took it.

items.head: Non-liability of banker receiving payment of cheque
items.group: Chapter XIV — Of crossed cheques
items.gist: A banker who in good faith and without negligence receives payment for a customer of a crossed cheque incurs no liability to the true owner if the title proves defective; crediting the customer's account before receiving payment does not take away this protection.

items.head: Application of chapter to drafts
items.group: Chapter XIV — Of crossed cheques
items.gist: The provisions on crossed cheques apply to drafts as if the draft were a cheque.

items.head: Set of bills
items.group: Chapter XV — Of bills in sets
items.gist: A bill may be drawn in parts (a set), each numbered and referring to the others; all parts make one bill. The person who accepts or indorses parts to different persons is liable on each part as if it were a separate bill.

items.head: Holder of first acquired part entitled to all
items.group: Chapter XV — Of bills in sets
items.gist: As between holders of different parts of a set, the one who first acquired title to any part is entitled to the other parts and to the money.

items.head: Law governing liability of maker, acceptor or indorser of foreign instrument
items.group: Chapter XVI — Of international law
items.gist: In the absence of a contrary contract, such liability is governed by the law of the place where the instrument is made, accepted or indorsed.

items.head: Law of place of payment governs dishonour
items.group: Chapter XVI — Of international law
items.gist: Where a note, bill or cheque is payable in a different place, the law of the place of payment determines what is dishonour and what notice is sufficient.

items.head: Instrument made etc. out of India but in accordance with Indian law
items.group: Chapter XVI — Of international law
items.gist: If such an instrument is made according to Indian law, a later dealing with it in India does not make it invalid because it is not in accordance with the foreign law.

items.head: Presumption as to foreign law
items.group: Chapter XVI — Of international law
items.gist: The law of any foreign country regarding promissory notes, bills and cheques is presumed to be the same as Indian law, unless proved otherwise.

items.head: Dishonour of cheque for insufficiency, etc., of funds in the account
items.group: Chapter XVII — Penalties in case of dishonour of certain cheques for insufficiency of funds
items.gist: Where a cheque drawn for discharge of a legally enforceable debt or liability is returned unpaid for insufficient funds or exceeding the arrangement, the drawer commits an offence punishable with imprisonment up to two years, or fine up to twice the amount, or both — provided the cheque was presented within its validity (3 months), the payee gave written notice of demand within 30 days of receiving information of dishonour, and the drawer failed to pay within 15 days of receiving the notice.

items.head: Presumption in favour of holder
items.group: Chapter XVII — Penalties in case of dishonour of certain cheques for insufficiency of funds
items.gist: It is presumed, unless the contrary is proved, that the holder received the cheque for the discharge, in whole or part, of any debt or other liability.

items.head: Defence which may not be allowed
items.group: Chapter XVII — Penalties in case of dishonour of certain cheques for insufficiency of funds
items.gist: It is no defence that the drawer had no reason to believe, when he issued the cheque, that it might be dishonoured on presentment.

items.head: Offences by companies
items.group: Chapter XVII — Penalties in case of dishonour of certain cheques for insufficiency of funds
items.gist: Every person in charge of and responsible to the company for the conduct of its business at the time is deemed guilty, unless he proves the offence was without his knowledge or that he exercised due diligence; directors nominated by the Government or a government financial corporation are not liable.

items.head: Cognizance of offences
items.group: Chapter XVII — Penalties in case of dishonour of certain cheques for insufficiency of funds
items.gist: Cognizance only on a written complaint by the payee or holder in due course, made within one month of the cause of action (delay may be condoned for sufficient cause), before a Metropolitan Magistrate or Judicial Magistrate First Class. Jurisdiction (2015): where the cheque is delivered for collection through an account — the court where the payee's bank branch is; otherwise, where the drawer's branch is.

items.head: Validation for transfer of pending cases
items.group: Chapter XVII — Penalties in case of dishonour of certain cheques for insufficiency of funds
items.gist: Pending cases are transferred to the court having jurisdiction under S.142(2); all later complaints against the same drawer go to the court where the first case is pending.

items.head: Power of court to try cases summarily
items.group: Chapter XVII — Penalties in case of dishonour of certain cheques for insufficiency of funds
items.gist: Offences under this Chapter are tried summarily; the trial should be concluded within six months from filing of the complaint as far as possible.

items.head: Power to direct interim compensation
items.group: Chapter XVII — Penalties in case of dishonour of certain cheques for insufficiency of funds
items.gist: The trial court may order the drawer to pay interim compensation up to 20 per cent of the cheque amount, within 60 days (extendable by 30); it is refundable with interest if he is acquitted.

items.head: Mode of service of summons
items.group: Chapter XVII — Penalties in case of dishonour of certain cheques for insufficiency of funds
items.gist: Summons may be served by speed post or approved courier; an endorsement of refusal is deemed service.

items.head: Evidence on affidavit
items.group: Chapter XVII — Penalties in case of dishonour of certain cheques for insufficiency of funds
items.gist: The complainant's evidence may be given by affidavit; the court may summon the person for examination.

items.head: Bank's slip prima facie evidence of certain facts
items.group: Chapter XVII — Penalties in case of dishonour of certain cheques for insufficiency of funds
items.gist: The bank's slip or memo marking the cheque dishonoured is presumed proof of the fact of dishonour, unless disproved.

items.head: Offences to be compoundable
items.group: Chapter XVII — Penalties in case of dishonour of certain cheques for insufficiency of funds
items.gist: Every offence under this Act is compoundable.

items.head: Power of appellate court to order payment pending appeal
items.group: Chapter XVII — Penalties in case of dishonour of certain cheques for insufficiency of funds
items.gist: In an appeal against conviction under S.138, the appellate court may order the appellant to deposit at least 20 per cent of the fine or compensation awarded by the trial court.
